body: Training LLM agents on long-horizon interactive tasks with reinforcement learning typically relies on human-annotated tasks and reliable verification, both expensive to construct for stateful environments. Self-play offers an alternative, but must generate achievable, compositional tasks and provide feedback beyond binary outcomes. We propose Explorer-Zero, a self-play framework that jointly generates tasks and fine-grained, verifiable rewards through environment interaction. A learned proposer explores the environment, constructs tasks, and records intermediate and final states as verification targets. These checkpoints reward partial completion, while alternating proposer--solver training adapts the generated curriculum. We show theoretically that subtask rewards reduce collapse among unsuccessful rollouts when they complete different numbers of subtasks. Without human-annotated training tasks, Explorer-Zero outperforms the evaluated self-play baselines across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and AppWorld; on AppWorld, our 30B agent reaches 59.67% task success, approaching 62.65% for RL on human-annotated tasks. Further analyses support task-relevant composition and benefits on complex tasks, while self-play initialization improves subsequent human-data RL across all three benchmarks.
summaryZh: 本文提出了Explorer-Zero，一种用于训练长程任务智能体的自博弈框架。该系统通过环境交互联合生成任务与细粒度的可验证奖励，无需依赖昂贵的人工标注数据。通过学习型提议者与求解者的交替训练，智能体能够有效探索环境并完成复杂任务。实验表明，该方法在多个基准测试中表现优异，证明了自博弈在构建复杂智能体任务中的潜力。

glossary.explanationZh: 智能体通过与自身或环境交互进行自我博弈以提升能力的方法。
指需要多个步骤、较长时间才能完成的复杂任务。
通过奖励机制引导智能体学习最优策略的机器学习方法。
指任务由多个子任务或组件构成，具有组合性。
智能体在环境中执行一系列动作的过程。
